newsitem.title: UK: North Sea mixed as Oseberg sells higher, Dated steady.
newsitem.headline: North Sea mixed as Oseberg sells higher, Dated steady.

text.p: North Sea crudes were mixed on Monday with signs that some grades might be on the mend while others continued to flounder.

Dated Brent was steady in a trade at Dec -48 cents for an end-November cargo. Whether the price, unchanged for some days now, reflects fundamentals or trading strategy linked to pricing on related markets remains difficult to tell, traders said.
Gas oil-rich Oseberg traded higher at Dated Brent +26 cents while Forties appeared to lose ground in a sale at Dated +17.
Unconfirmed reports were that Forties also moved at premium in the twenties over Brent.
Intermonth spreads slipped with outright losses with Dec/Jan done at +25 cents after an early deal at +31 cents.
CFDs reflected Dated's failure to move higher and were offered at Jan -5 cents, or Dec -30.

Nigerian crudes for early/mid December were steady around a mid-40 cent premium over Brent for light grades and mid-50 cents for Forcados. Some remaining November crude and concerns over the possibility of non-performance on one or two December cargoes were keeping a lid on differentials.
A U.S. major with a VLCC of Qua Iboe on the water was likely to take the crude into the Med, dealers said.
End-Nov Brass River and Escravos were also still available. But the Dec 1-20 period has already seen Forcados sold out.
Most dealers were expecting one or two extra December spot Qua Iboe cargoes on the market as a result of non-performance.
But concerns that five or six might be made available were widely dismissed.
Urals in the Med was helped by expected maintenance at Black Sea terminal Novorossiisk and was pegged at Brent -70 cents cif Med, in line with a sale on Friday.
